solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Marine holding yours truly back with a bloody problem

indicators.note: holding means the first word wraps around the next piece, keeping it inside
back tells us to read the pronoun piece from right to left

blocks.note: thalassic means of the sea
yours truly is the speaker, me

explanation.surface: A sea creature or sailor clutching the writer, suffering some gory trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marine' looks like a soldier or the definition; it is the adjective thalassic, of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Thalassemia is an inherited blood disorder, so a sufferer has a genuine blood-related condition.

clue.text: Nonsense line abandoned by Dublin party

indicators.note: something abandoned is left out, so the party word loses that letter

blocks.note: L is the usual abbreviation for line
a hooley is a lively Irish party

explanation.surface: A party in Dublin where somebody's chat-up line falls flat as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: HOOLEY without its L leaves HOOEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooey is slang for rubbish talk, empty foolish claims or humbug.

clue.text: Everyone new is in in good time only once

indicators.note: is in places the abbreviation for new inside the word for punctual

blocks.note: everyone is all
N is the abbreviation for new
in good time means early

explanation.surface: Everyone arriving punctually, it seems, with a new person turning up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' marks the definition as an obsolete Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Allenarly is an old Scots adverb meaning solely or exclusively, hence the archaic flag.

clue.text: Still very angry when hotel’s lacking

indicators.note: lacking says a letter is missing from the word for furious

blocks.note: hairless is slang for extremely angry
H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet; the 's is short for is

explanation.surface: A guest is still furious because the hotel is short of something.
explanation.walkthrough: Chambers gives hairless as slang for furious; dropping its H leaves AIRLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Still air has no breeze, and an airless day is calm, close and windless.

clue.text: Seen running on railway showing disdain

indicators.note: running suggests letters set in motion and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: Someone spotted running along the railway line looks scornful.
explanation.definitionFit: Sneery describes a contemptuous, mocking manner, the look of a scornful person.

clue.text: Tourist publication’s not good in Scots onscreen edition

indicators.note: not says the following word is taken out of the travel book

blocks.note: a guidebook is written for tourists; the 's is short for is
guid is the Scots spelling of good

explanation.surface: A travel guide is criticised as poor in its Scottish screen version.
explanation.walkthrough: GUIDEBOOK loses GUID, leaving EBOOK.
explanation.definitionFit: An ebook is a digital version of a book read on a device's display.

clue.text: Girl loving criminal way of working lines

blocks.note: MO is modus operandi, a way of working
LL is the abbreviation for lines

explanation.surface: A girl who adores a crook explains his method and his lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal way of working' looks like one phrase for MO; 'criminal' actually belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A moll is a gangster's female companion or girlfriend in slang.

clue.text: Seized Conservative reportedly let out

indicators.note: reportedly means we go by how the phrase is spoken, not spelt

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
let out, as a secret, is leaked

explanation.surface: A Tory grabbed after news of something got out.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleek is a Scots verb meaning to grab or catch hold of, as with a hook.

clue.text: Initially trace extinct old wild ox, smaller, lacking in character?

indicators.note: initially asks for just the opening letter of the next word

blocks.note: the first letter of trace
ext. is the dictionary abbreviation for extinct
the ure is the urus or aurochs, an extinct wild ox
less means smaller

explanation.surface: Tracking down a long-gone wild ox proves a dull, flavourless pursuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Character here means feel or grain, so something without surface quality has no texture.

clue.text: Passes round line in letter of gratitude

indicators.note: round says the mountain gaps surround the next two pieces

blocks.note: cols are mountain passes
L is the abbreviation for line
taken as written

explanation.surface: A thank-you note is handed around with a line written inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A collins is a thank-you note sent to a host after a stay, named after Mr Collins in Pride and Prejudice.

clue.text: Good-natured about empty local pub numbers limitation?

indicators.note: empty means the inside of the word is cleared, keeping just its ends
about places the kindly word around the other pieces

blocks.note: good-natured means caring
the outside letters of local
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: Pleasant regulars hang about a deserted neighbourhood pub to swap figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Numbers' suggests figures or songs; here it means telephone numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Call barring blocks certain phone numbers from being dialled, a restriction on calls.

clue.text: Be driven by wind power in swim round Cape Wrath

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the word for swim

blocks.note: soom is Scots for swim, and Cape Wrath is in the far north of Scotland
P is the abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A sailing boat is pushed along by the wind off a Scottish headland.
explanation.walkthrough: P goes inside S|OOM; 'round Cape Wrath' just flags the Scottish word.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoom is an old sailing verb for scudding before the wind under little canvas.

clue.text: Alley in Scotland attracting English mathematician

blocks.note: an alley is a playing marble, and bool is the Scots word for a marble or bowl
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A narrow Scottish lane draws in an English scholar of numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alley' looks like a lane, but here it is a marble.
explanation.definitionFit: George Boole was the English mathematician who founded Boolean algebra and symbolic logic.

clue.text: US president keeping vote lead in east, not a full digit

indicators.note: lead in means the opening letter of the following word
keeping means the leader's word holds the other pieces inside

blocks.note: prex is US college slang for a president
a poll is a vote
the first letter of east

explanation.surface: An American president holds a ballot lead in the eastern states.
explanation.walkthrough: POLLE goes inside PRE|X. Prex is American slang for the president of a college, not of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A prepollex is a rudimentary extra digit found beside the thumb in some animals.

clue.text: Smear with dung left with urine on the turn

indicators.note: on the turn means the word for urine is turned round, read backwards

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
pee is urine

explanation.surface: Farmyard muck left along with some souring urine.
explanation.definitionFit: Leep, from Hindi, means to plaster a floor or wall with cow manure.

clue.text: Outlaw party always carries large ammo belt

indicators.note: carries says the party and always pieces hold a letter between them

blocks.note: to outlaw is to ban
a do is a party
L is the abbreviation for large
e'er is the poetic form of ever, always

explanation.surface: A gang of outlaws always carry a big belt of bullets.
explanation.walkthrough: E'er is the poetic contraction of ever.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandoleer is a shoulder belt with loops or pockets holding cartridges.

clue.text: Linen once worn by northern girl

indicators.note: worn by suggests the fabric wraps around the next letter as clothing does

blocks.note: lyne is an obsolete word for linen
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: Old-fashioned linen clothing worn by a girl from the North.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes inside LYN|E.
explanation.definitionFit: Lynne is a female first name, so any woman called that fits.

clue.text: Giant bird and northern jackdaw look finally united fighting kite

indicators.note: finally picks only the closing letter of the word before it

blocks.note: rok is a variant spelling of roc, the giant bird of legend
ka is a northern dialect word for jackdaw
the last letter of look
U is the abbreviation for united

explanation.surface: A huge bird and a jackdaw join together to battle a kite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kite' looks like another bird to join the roc and jackdaw; here it is the toy.
explanation.definitionFit: A rokkaku is a six-sided Japanese kite flown in competitions to cut down rivals.

clue.text: Ill-mannered bodyguards interrupting speech

indicators.note: interrupting means the guards break into the middle of the next word

blocks.note: a say is a chance to speak
the SS were Hitler's bodyguard corps

explanation.surface: Rude minders cutting in on someone's address.
explanation.definitionFit: Sassy means cheeky or impudent, showing a disrespectful lack of manners.

clue.text: Son drunk made out

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
canned is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A son who was drunk got away with it, or claimed to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made out' looks like kissing or pretending; here it means perceived.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan the horizon is to look closely and discern, so scanned means perceived.

clue.text: Local girl taking in a single drifter

indicators.note: taking in means the girl's word holds the next piece inside it

blocks.note: mor is a dialect word for a girl
a single is one

explanation.surface: A girl from the area puts up a lone wanderer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' signals a dialect word rather than a girl from nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: To moon about is to wander aimlessly and dreamily, so a mooner is an idle wanderer.

clue.text: Men eat with European minister just appointed

blocks.note: OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers
to dine is to eat
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Soldiers dine alongside a European clergyman newly installed.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinee is someone being or newly ordained, a freshly made deacon or priest.

clue.text: All through the middle part of ball game

indicators.note: the middle part means the first and last letters are cut away

blocks.note: lacrosse is a game played with a ball and netted sticks

explanation.surface: Someone tours the centre of a stadium during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: LACROSSE loses its outer L and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Across means from one side to the other, covering the whole width.

clue.text: Find out about English literary doctor

indicators.note: about means the word for work out goes around the next letter

blocks.note: to suss is to work out
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Research uncovers an English medic who writes books.
explanation.walkthrough: E goes inside S|USS.
explanation.definitionFit: Dr Seuss was the pen name of children's author Theodor Geisel, a doctor only in name.

clue.text: A small coin Germany declared out of use

blocks.note: taken as written
a red cent is the smallest coin, so red stands for a tiny coin
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A German coin has been withdrawn from circulation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of use' looks like part of the coin story; it marks the definition as an obsolete word.
explanation.definitionFit: Aredd is an archaic past tense of aread, meaning announced, counselled or made known.

clue.text: Decision about one Eastender

indicators.note: about means the ruling goes around the next letter

blocks.note: an arret is a judgment or decree of a court
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A ruling concerning a single resident of east London.
explanation.walkthrough: An Eastender is a Londoner from the East End, where Harriet is said without its H.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Arriet is the stock name for a Cockney woman, from dropping the first letter of Harriet.

clue.text: Racing driver unfortunate during last reversing

indicators.note: during puts the word for unlucky inside the word for last
reversing means the combined letters are read backwards

blocks.note: the rear is the last part
ill can mean unlucky, as in ill fortune

explanation.surface: An unlucky driver comes last while backing up.
explanation.definitionFit: A rallier competes in rallies, motor races over public roads and tracks.

clue.text: Can whale be relative newcomer to North America?

blocks.note: can ... be asks whether something is, so read it as is
the sei is a species of rorqual whale

explanation.surface: A question whether a whale species has only lately reached American waters.
explanation.definitionFit: Issei are first-generation Japanese immigrants to the United States and Canada, so fairly recent arrivals.

clue.text: Asian plant Henry fed to pet pig

indicators.note: fed to means the name's letter is put inside the next word

blocks.note: doll is an endearment for a pet or darling
H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Someone called Henry feeds a pet pig some foreign greenery.
explanation.walkthrough: H goes inside D|OLL.
explanation.definitionFit: Dholl is the pigeon pea, a legume grown across South Asia for its seeds.

clue.text: Miss old comic abandoned by clubs

indicators.note: abandoned by says the comedian's name is left without that letter

blocks.note: John Cleese is the Monty Python comedian
C is the abbreviation for clubs in cards

explanation.surface: A veteran comedian is dropped by the nightclubs.
explanation.walkthrough: CLEESE without C. 'Old' flags the definition as archaic, so 'old comic' is a false pairing.
explanation.definitionFit: Leese is an obsolete Spenserian verb meaning to lose, so it can mean fail to keep.

clue.text: Old man’s second free ticket

blocks.note: old man is a father, pa, and the 's adds S
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: Dad's second complimentary ticket.
explanation.definitionFit: A pass grants admission or travel without payment, a complimentary permit.

clue.text: Keep at a distance from most of navy

indicators.note: most of means the last letter of the naval word is dropped

blocks.note: a fleet is a navy

explanation.surface: A ship holds back from most of the fleet.
explanation.definitionFit: To flee something is to run away from it and avoid it.

clue.text: While doing something else with old metal and silk thread

blocks.note: in can mean with, as in a man in a hat
passing was a thread of gold or silver wound around silk

explanation.surface: Embroidery with antique gilt wire and silk.
explanation.definitionFit: Mentioning something in passing means doing it incidentally, as a side remark.

clue.text: Called on to retire, we finally expire suddenly

indicators.note: to retire is to go back, so the word for called on is read backwards
finally picks the closing letter of the word before it

blocks.note: a visitor is seen when they call on someone
the last letter of we

explanation.surface: Visited by friends before turning in, we die quite unexpectedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expire' looks like dying, but it means breathe out.
explanation.definitionFit: Neese is an old form of sneeze, a sudden involuntary blast of breath.

clue.text: Female looking ahead before cutting historic tax

indicators.note: cutting means the word for before slices into the tax word

blocks.note: sess is an old form of cess, a tax
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A woman planning ahead before reducing an old levy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' looks like a position word for the charade; it supplies the old word ere.
explanation.definitionFit: A seeress is a woman prophet who foresees future events.

clue.text: Dug up something deposited in spring in grave, dead?

indicators.note: in places the mineral word inside the word for grim

blocks.note: grave means dire, very serious
sinter is the mineral crust left around hot springs
D is the abbreviation for dead

explanation.surface: Something buried in a grave as spring came, a dead body, is exhumed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grave' looks like a burial place but means serious.
explanation.definitionFit: Disinterred means removed from a grave, exhumed and brought back up.
